claim.quote: No evidence for $\nu_{\mu} \to \nu_{s}$ transitions is found and we set a world-leading limit on $\theta_{24}$ for values of $\Delta m^{2}_{41} \lesssim 1\,\mathrm{eV}^{2}$.

date.quote: Search for Sterile Neutrinos Mixing with Muon Neutrinos in MINOS

key_value_text.quote: We constrain the mixing parameters θ₂₄ and Δm²₄₁ and set limits on parameters of the four-dimensional Pontecorvo-Maki-Nakagawa-Sakata matrix
key_value_text.value: Upper limit on the θ₂₄ mixing angle for Δm²₄₁ ≲ 1 eV² (described by the paper as world-leading), from a νμ-dominated beam over 1.04 km and 735 km baselines with 10.56×10²⁰ protons on target; no evidence for νμ→νs oscillations

name: Search for Sterile Neutrinos Mixing with Muon Neutrinos in MINOS
notes: experiment_ids lists both experiment:minos and experiment:minos-plus because the analysis uses the combined MINOS/MINOS+ near+far detector data set (1.04 km and 735 km baselines) described in the abstract.

significance.locator: arXiv:1607.01176, abstract (no significance/sigma reported for a null/limit result)
significance.note: An exclusion-limit result: no signal was observed, so no discovery significance is reported.

summary.plain: MINOS searched for muon neutrinos turning into undetectable 'sterile' neutrinos, over distances of 1.04 and 735 kilometres, and found no evidence of it. The paper sets what it calls a world-leading limit on the mixing angle θ24 for small mass splittings (Δm²41 up to about 1 eV²).
summary.technical: Two-detector search for νμ→νs oscillations over 1.04 km and 735 km baselines using a νμ-dominated beam peaked at 3 GeV (10.56×10²⁰ POT) and a one-sterile-neutrino model, under the assumption that νe-νs mixing is negligible (|U_e4|²=0); no evidence for νμ→νs transitions is found, and the paper sets what it calls a world-leading limit on θ₂₄ for Δm²₄₁ ≲ 1 eV².

title: Search for Sterile Neutrinos Mixing with Muon Neutrinos in MINOS
why_it_matters: The paper's introduction lists the LSND and MiniBooNE excesses, the reactor anomaly and the gallium-source deficit as anomalous oscillation signals that may potentially be reconciled with the three-flavor picture by adding one or more sterile neutrinos; this search found no evidence for νμ→νs transitions.
